body:
NAMED BY THE T174 BUILD LANE in comments rather than closed, which was the right scope call — both are
unreachable today. They are filed because a gap named only in a comment is not a work item, and both
become reachable the moment an adjacent feature lands.

PART A — A REGISTER GRANTEE JOINS THE TRUSTED-STRIKER SET.
`lawfulStrikersJson` (src/gateway/accounts.ts) builds the sub-view of authors whose negations bind, and
it selects grant-shaped deltas without narrowing on the VERB. A `register` grant is grant-shaped, so
its holder is admitted to the striker set.

INERT TODAY, and the reason matters: a striker's negations bind only for deltas that reach the
resolver, and a register grantee has no write standing, so it can append nothing. Nothing it signs is
ingested, so nothing it signs can suppress.

REACHABLE WHEN: federation ingest admits deltas by that key. §8's admission is a policy over authors;
a store whose trust policy admits a connector's key would then be admitting a key that is ALSO in the
striker set, and a strike it signed would suppress the operator's claims for every reader. That is H1's
shape arriving through a door nobody was watching.

WHY IT WAS NOT CLOSED IN T174: narrowing the sub-view means moving the bytes of an EXPORTED gather
body, which is a wire-visible change to a term other stores may hold. That wants its own change with
its own migration question answered, not a rider on an authority verb.

THE WORK: narrow `lawfulStrikersJson` to grants whose verb is one that confers striking, and decide
which verbs those are — today `admin` plainly, `write` arguably, `register` plainly not. Then answer
the §20 question: does the changed gather body count as a breaking on-wire change, and if so what
migration carries a store that holds the old term.
RAIL: a register grantee's negation does NOT suppress an operator claim for any reader, asserted at
both levels — the delta is present, and a reader through a Schema still sees the operator's claim —
with a live bystander proving an `admin` grantee's strike still binds.

PART B — A REGISTER GRANT SURVIVES AN UNBIND.
`survivingWriteGrantIds` (src/gateway/container.ts) collects grants to strike when a connection is
unbound, and it filters on the `write` verb alone. A register grant held by the same key is not
collected, so it survives an unbind that was meant to remove that key's standing entirely.

UNREACHABLE TODAY because nothing mints a register grant on a connection key — T174's grant is minted
by the operator against a connector's actor, and the unbind path handles connection keys.

REACHABLE WHEN: a connection can be granted registration, which is exactly what T174 makes thinkable
and a follow-up may make real. The failure would be silent and in the dangerous direction: an operator
unbinds a connection, the report says it is unbound, and a register grant keeps working. That is H7 —
a report that can be false — on the revocation path.

THE WORK: collect EVERY verb the key holds rather than a named one, or state in the function's own
comment which verbs it deliberately leaves and why. Prefer the first: a revocation that names a subset
is a revocation whose report overclaims.
RAIL: unbinding a connection strikes every grant that key holds, whatever the verb, two-sided with a
bystander key whose grants survive.

BOTH PARTS: repair tier when built — each makes a report or a fence more honest and widens nothing.
title: A register grant confers striking it should not, and survives an unbind that should take it
